Iwaniska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Iwaniska, Poland

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Iwaniska's Jewish community, first documented in 1578, made up 54.15 percent of the town's population by 1921, most killed at Treblinka in the fall of 1942. This cemetery was also used to bury religious books hidden before the ghetto's liquidation; both graves and books were later plundered by the local population for building material. In 2006, the site was cleaned and fenced with a stone wall incorporating recovered matzevot fragments.
